claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr is a single-phase BCC alloy.
The constituent atoms in WTaTiVZr are randomly arranged.
Commercially pure tungsten has a BCC structure.
Commercially pure tungsten lacks significant pre-existing lattice distortion relative to WTaTiVZr.
Random occupancy by dissimilar refractory atoms produces significant lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr raises the energy barriers for dislocation motion.
Raised barriers to dislocation motion cause WTaTiVZr to activate additional slip systems.
Activation of additional slip systems distributes plastic strain more homogeneously in WTaTiVZr.
Slip activity in pure tungsten is more localized than in WTaTiVZr.
Localized slip in pure tungsten causes earlier crack initiation and lower toughness.
At 800–1200°C, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater ductility than commercially pure tungsten under otherwise identical loading conditions.
At 800–1200°C, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater toughness than commercially pure tungsten under otherwise identical loading conditions.
WTaTiVZr will develop more uniform dislocation networks than pure tungsten.
Crack initiation will be delayed in WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
The proposed behavior is applicable between 800°C and 1200°C at controlled strain rates in inert atmospheres or vacuum.
Thermal or environmental factors outside the stated test window may alter the behavior.
A quantitative correlation should exist between lattice distortion and homogeneous slip, plastic strain, and toughness in WTaTiVZr.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says lattice distortion raises barriers to dislocation motion, whereas the falsification rule frames the expected effect as enhanced dislocation mobility. Homogeneous slip activity is not equivalent to increased mobility, so the direction of the claimed dislocation-level effect is internally ambiguous.
